sentences: Parity is a basic function that small constant-depth classical circuits cannot approximate well on uniformly random inputs.
This project asks whether a shallow quantum preprocessing stage can remove that limitation when its measured output is passed to a classical AC0 circuit.
The conjecture concerns constant-depth quantum circuits with bounded-fan-in gates, followed by the specified classical postprocessing.
Any approximation guarantee must account for both the random input and the randomness of quantum measurement.
Establishing the conjecture would place a concrete limit on hybrid computation and help clarify the power of weak classical procedures that use shallow quantum devices.
